utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-08-91-T. The Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to you all. May I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. On behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor, I'm Tom Hannis joined by our Case Manager, Crispian Smith, and today we have two of our interns who have been working with us; Mr. Guillermo Otalora Lozano and Ms. Ana Trstenjak. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan, and Tatjana Savic our Case Manager appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Expert has left The Hague, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Igor Pantelic for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we bring the witness in. Mr. Zecevic, I think you have 582 documents still to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the list, Your Honour. That is not the factual situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. And what is the factual situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure at this point, but I think less than 150 documents we need to show to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. And where --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Probably less than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Where will that take us?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we believe that we will need another day to deal with this witness in addition to our time, the time that we have, plus another day, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Nielsen's report is very dense document, as you can see, and highly relevant. It touches the very issues in this case, and I think we need to in order to assist the Trial Chamber and definitely shorten our Defence case, we are trying to establish some of the issues with Mr. Nielsen here, if that would be possible, of course. And -- but in any case, we need to challenge his report because it's the basis, as I say, to the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution with which we take the issue. Therefore, I kindly ask you to give us additional time, I think this would be of assistance to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In that regard may I, at the end the day, could we recess two or three minutes early just to assess how much longer they think they are going to need with him, because it's going to affect our planning for scheduling next week and maybe we can confer with the witness on the record about his availability dates as well, because it sounds like he may have to come back for three days, one more day of Mr. Zecevic, one day of Mr. Pantelic, and at least maybe one day of redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Next week, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll be available, Your Honour. I'm not sure you can get unanimity on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I have two observations to put to you in respect of your application for more time. Let me start off by saying that I'm not in any way opposed to giving you the time you need, but first of all is there a way in which you can think of having the many documents admitted without having to go through so many of them? I'm especially referring to the model that we applied with an earlier witness to try to group them together which might reduce the time you need actually in court to confront the witness with the many documents. That's one question. And the other question is that without in any way trying to interfere with the way you conduct your examination -- your cross-examination, sorry, I've noticed that many of the questions you put could actually be saved. Like when you ask the witnesses, not particularly this witness, this doesn't go for you, it goes for the Prosecution and for Mr. Pantelic as well, ascertaining from the witness whether you have read out a passage correctly is perhaps not always necessary. So my quest is really are for all parties to focus their examination-in-chief and their cross-examination more directly and strongly to -- in order to reach the point that you wish to get to. But let me turn to my first question, if you have any idea of how you can get through the many documents in a quicker way?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours I'm thankful for your suggestion. I think definitely the way how to proceed would be the already established practice in this trial, that we group the documents, and then I would ask the witness on one or two documents and then offer the group of the documents for admittance. Your Honours, I'm perfectly willing to follow your suggestion, but what I'm trying to do is basically focus, trying to assist the Trial Chamber by focusing the parts of the document that in our opinion are relevant and -- and are going into the heart of the matter in this case. Therefore, I believe I'm assisting Trial Chamber at the very end because it doesn't -- the Trial Chamber would not need to go to -- some of the documents are, Your Honours, 400, 500 pages, so we -- I was actually, I'm trying actually follow your suggestion that we really focus on the parts of documents that are relevant to our case. But I can follow your advice which you suggested right now and just ask the witness more directly, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let's try that, see how it works out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. And bench will think on and discuss your application for one day more during the break when the three of us are here. That reminds me for the record, we are sitting pursuant to Article 15 bis, Judge Hall being absent. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have nothing, Your Honour it's up to Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I've' very sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cordially wish you good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment, Mr. Nielsen. I may remind you that you are still under your oath. A formality, but I have to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, yesterday before the end of the last session, I showed you a document 1D78, a dispatch dated 1 April 1992, referring to the collegium meeting of the MUP held on that day, and I've been informed that the status of this document in e-court has now been clarified. So it's 1D78. And on page 4915 you told me you had no occasion to see a single document which would lead you to conclude that the division of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina was peaceful and with the consent and approval of the -- of all parties. Isn't it the case that this document, 1D78, shows precisely that, that the division of the MUP was peaceful and conducted with the considered approval of the leadership of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I noted yesterday, I cite a version of this document in my report, and I agree with you that this particular document indicates that - according to this document alone - that the division of the MUP was peaceful and conducted with the approval of the leadership of the MUP, again minus the minister, which I find very important. And I also would point out that there are a host of documents which I cite in my report including documents from Bosnian Serbs after 31 March 1992 which conclusively demonstrate that the division of the MUP was not peaceful and was not conducted with the approval of the leadership of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, in this document on page 2 it is stated that attention is also accorded to the co-ordination of some joint services. Doesn't that mean joint services at the level of the central MUP in Sarajevo? Isn't it consistent with the defence case and with what we have shown you related it to the so-called Cutileiro plan?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If viewed in isolation, yes, it is. However, I again point out that having been able to review this, I note that at the various time that this collegium was meeting, the minister, Alija Delimustafic was meeting with the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina to discuss the contradictory dispatches of Mr. Mandic and Mr. Delimustafic of the previous day, 31 March 1992. And I would refer you to the SRBiH MUP rule book, Articles 118 to 124 which indicate quite clearly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. -- slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you, Your Honour. And in Articles 118 to 124 of the SRBiH MUP rule book which deal with the workings of this collegium of SRBiH MUP, it emerges that the minister plays a critical role. Let's be honest, they are not discussing how many office supplies they want to order for the rest of 1992. They discussing the disintegration and division of the ministry, and I think it is extraordinary that they would take this decision in the absence of the minister when is he in fact meeting with the government to discuss that very point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, I would appreciate it very much if you could concentrate on the question I'm actually asking because you are going too much ahead and I want you to answer step by step about all these important things. When I showed you this document on transcript page 4916, you said exactly what you've repeated now. Could you give me a reference for that document you are citing in your report because in the part that is subtitled disintegration of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, your paragraphs 78 through 94, I could not find that reference when you say that it's a version of this document 1D78?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, sir. I cite a version of that document in footnote 196 on page 54 and I refer there to the document bearing the ERN P004-4289, P004-4289A, which in large part reproduces the document that you are talking about, and that we were looking at here on the screen. I agree with you and I'm very thankful to my esteemed colleague Dr. Bajagic for reminding me of this document's existence, and I agree with you that I should also have cited this document, but I do cite a version of it in footnote 196.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, you are citing that in paragraph 193, your footnote 196, but it does not explain the so-called solemn declaration which you misinterpret and misrepresent as an oath of loyalty. You don't make any reference in that paragraph to this document and its connection with the disintegration of the MUP; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not make a reference to this document in specific connection with the events of 31st March 1992 and 1 April 1992. However, if you were to pull up that document, you will see that it is in large part a reproduction of the document that you identify as 1D78.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, to conclude, when you were writing your report, and you said the same thing right now, I think you agreed with me now that it's a shortcoming of your report that this document 1D78 is not cited, and we don't have your position as an expert concerning that document, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree that it is a shortcoming.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, let us study now your position concerning the presence of Minister Delimustafic. You drew our attention yesterday to the fact that Minister Delimustafic was not present at this collegium meeting. I asked you, isn't it true that the minister represents the ministry, and you answered, not only the ministry, but also the cabinet to which he belongs. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the government to which he belongs and the ministry, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. It was interpreted as cabinet, it's about the same thing. Tell me, Mr. Nielsen, isn't it the case that the then government of Bosnia-Herzegovina was a coalition government of the SDS, the SDA, and the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the SDS had appointed eight ministers, SDA eight ministers, and the HDZ four ministers?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the exact composition of the government at that time but that's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will now show you a chart, a schematic prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's document 10138.4 in e-court. If the usher could give you a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is an organisational chart of the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the period January 1991 through March 1992. It was created at the Office of the Prosecutor, our learned friends on the other side, and I would like to discuss it with you. Isn't it true that in the ministry along with the minister there is one deputy minister and nine assistant ministers?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, you are certainly aware that under the law and in accordance with the nature of things, the deputy minister stands in for the minister when the minister is unable to attend?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly that is the case. That's the point of a deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This meeting, this collegium, in the political jargon collegium meant the meeting of the most senior leaders in the ministry. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the SRBiH MUP rule book says; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you about political jargon, I meant to say that applied to all the other ministries, not only of the interior, the Ministry of Agriculture, the Ministry of Justice, et cetera. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have similar expertise on other ministries in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time, but it would not surprise me if other ministries had similar bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So at this collegium on the 1st of April, 1992, document 1D78, out of nine assistant ministers, seven attended. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I won't second guess your math, but that's probably correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, out of nine assistants, seven were present; namely, two from the HDZ, Mr. Bruno Stojic and Mr. Branko Kvesic; three assistant ministers appointed by the SDA, Mr. Avdo Hebib, Jusuf Pusina, and Akif Sabic and two from the SDS, and the deputy minister, Mr. Zepinic. Aren't you going to agree with me that it is a very respectable attendance for the collegium?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that it's a considerable attendance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You will also agree with me that collegium meetings were also held without the minister, you see many collegium meetings that you cite in your report of the MUP of Republika Srpska where Mico Stanisic did not attend or attended part of the time and then his deputy took over?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And to conclude on this document, although this very respectable attendance, as you accepted and the discussion of the collegium you did not take this document into account and you accepted it's a shortcoming, but you will agree with me that the role of the expert in trial proceedings is to assist the Trial Chamber with his specific knowledge and information in an objective and unbiased way; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That conforms to my understanding of the role of the expert, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you will agree with me that omitting this document from an expert report could not really be considered as an expression of objectivity?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, it's argumentative.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you said yesterday on page 4921 and confirmed the same thing this morning, that if this document would have to be looked in isolation, you would understand how I reached a conclusion that I presented to you yesterday, namely that the division of the MUP was carried out with the consent of all the relevant bodies and individuals in the ministry, but then you said looking from the point of view of all the documents that you had an occasion to see, you cannot agree with my conclusion. Do you primarily mean all the letters written by minister Delimustafic when you say that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, not at all. I primarily mean that this document is fully and richly contradicted by the RS MUP's officials themselves who subsequently refer to the, and I stress once again this is their own word, the illegal organisation of Serbian personnel in the seat of SRBiH MUP, the illegal arming of Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina by employees of SRBiH MUP, and they state very clearly in their own 1992 draft annual report that this culminated -- this illegal - and again for the umpteenth time, I stress that this is their word - in the illegal -- it's just that this culminated in the -- this illegal action culminated in the sending of Mr. Mandic's 31 March dispatch. I also would note that in a television programme in January 1993, Tomislav Kovac who was intimately involved in this business, referred to the fact that the Bosnian Serbs had, and I quote, destroyed SRBiH MUP. And I also would finally refer at this stage to Mr. Mandic himself who on 5th May 1992, told his former colleague Brana Kvesic, and I will here for the sake of accuracy please quote it directly in B/C/S, he said to Mr. Kvesic, and I'm now shifting to B/C/S [Interpretation] "When I sent that dispatch, I fucked up the whole MUP." [In English] End of quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you, Mr. Nielsen. Tell me, isn't it true that all your sources are actually secondary sources, as it were? Let me just explain. Did you ever come across a single statement by Mr. Mico Stanisic or one of his assistant, a statement about the division of the MUP in 1992 having been an illegal act? When you quoted a conversation between Kvesic and Mandic, it doesn't tell us anything about legality or illegality of this occurrence. Did you hear directly from any of the players word to the effect of such a qualification when it comes to the division of the MUP in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will state very clearly that I have not come across such a statement by Mr. Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, I have come across a large number of such statements from key participants other than Mr. Stanisic and as a historian, I clearly consider the RS MUP report produced by the RS MUP itself a primary source, not a secondary source.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, you spent a certain time in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, you speak the language, you will agree with me, won't you, that among the population of the former Yugoslavia there is a trend of blowing things out of proportion after a certain lapse of time and that they tend to give things a different connotation than the one that is actually attached to them and actually exists?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I would like to engage in such stereotyping.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Nielsen, isn't it true that the agreement was reached at the level of all the three ethnically based parties within the MUP about the MUP division, and that the division was in keeping with that agreement and that it was also done in -- bearing in mind the Cutileiro agreement and that only after that Mr. Alija Delimustafic and the SDA because of their own reasons, reasons known to them, gave up on that agreement, will you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have to object, Your Honour. That's a compound question, there's at least three parts to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to break the question down.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the division of the Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP was based on the document that I showed to you and the facts that you are aware of, will you agree that that division received the consent of all the three parties, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the agreement existed with the SDA but that subsequently because of some other reasons, this SDA withdrew from that agreement and gave up on it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please be specific about which agreement we are referring to, because we are talking about several different agreements here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the agreement on the division of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my mind, if you are referring to the -- such an agreement as it was previewed in the Cutileiro framework of principles or statement of principles, then my answer is that, yes, I am aware that the SDA signed it. I'm also aware that the SDA representatives subsequently withdrew from that agreement, and, therefore, it was no longer valid from their point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We have already clarified that, we did it yesterday. But now I'm asking you this: Do you agree that the SDA first gave its consent to the division of the MUP as can be seen in 1D78, or rather, as we can conclude based on that document, and that subsequently the SDA gave up on that agreement, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have to object. I think that assumes facts that aren't in evidence yet. We have this document listing some MUP employees who were candidates that were proposed by the SDA, but we haven't established that when they are meeting in the collegium that they are representing the SDA. I think we need to establish something further before that question can be asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that we have already established that and that there's no need for us to waste anymore time on that. I've shown the organisational scheme of the ministry and within that scheme you can see who among the assistants belonged to what party, and I believe that that fact is not in dispute at that moment between the party to these proceedings. The three ethnically based parties are made up of all the relevant bodies in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including the Republican Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's my understanding of the chart that where it lists an individual, for example, Mr. Hebib, and it says SDA under his name, that means that he was a candidate that was proposed for that position by the SDA. It does not necessarily means he is a member of the SDA. I see your client is named on this chart as SDS, and I think he's taken the position he was not a member of the SDS so that's the point I want to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never said that they belonged to the SDA. I just -- I'm just stating that they pursued the SDA policies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I am sorry, I understood your earlier question to suggest that the SDA had agreed to this split based on the presence of Mr. Hebib and the others who were candidates of the SDA for those positions. And I don't think we've heard any evidence to establish that they were representing the SDA in these discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] In order to avoid wasting time, I believe that the matter is clear enough and there's no need for us to go over the same grounds again and again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Nielsen, in paragraph 93, your footnote 139, you state that Mr. Ganic, a Presidency member, stated at the beginning of April 1992 that all MUP employees who joined the MUP of Republika Srpska would be summarily dismissed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I say that he said that they should consider themselves permanently fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to show you 65 ter 77, but before that, let me show you 65 ter 67. This is a document which you offer as the only reference with regard to the collegium. This is your footnote 196, I believe we have just spoken about that.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document was issued by the Banja Luka Security Services Centre on the 3rd of April, 1992. And the collegium is quoted in the document and it is also stated that the Banja Luka Security Services Centre undertook measures in order to divide the MUP in keeping with the letter sent by the MUP of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina dated the 1st of April, and in keeping with the laws and constitution of Republika Srpska. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document says. The laws -- in keeping with the laws and constitution of Republika Srpska and not of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Also it is stated in here that the employees will voluntarily opt for either staying in the Republika Srpska MUP or not, and in that the new Law on the Establishment the Ministry of the Interior Republika Srpska, they were left with an option to stay performing the same duties as they did at the moment when that division became topical; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document says and that is why I cite it in footnote 196.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the very end of that document, a reference is made to the fact that all employees, I underline all employees, will be duty-bound to take solemn declaration and in this document, Chief Zupljanin remind everybody that the solemn declaration is identical to the one that was taken under the former Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is again an accurate rereading of the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document for admission, if there are no objections to that on the part of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D137, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 77. This is your footnote 161. I believe that it is document 52 under tab 52 in your binder. This is a letter sent by Minister Alija Delimustafic on the 10th of April, 1992. And in this letter, he informs all the addressees in the MUP of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina about the organisation of the Serbian MUP units, and he says that there has been pressure and blackmail on non-Serbs to sign some declaration of loyalty otherwise their posts will be terminated. It is true that that's what the document says and that is why you are quoting this document in your footnote 161, am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in your report you mostly use the term "loyalty pledge" rather than "solemn declaration," and the latter has been referred to in the law and that's how Mr. Zupljanin calls that statement in his letter; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term I use certainly, I believe, most in the report is the English word "oath" which I believe is translated into B/C/S in the version you have as "zakletva."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you have also introduced a new, a third term, "zakletvo" or oath. Under the law that you have analysed in great detail and from all the documents, we can see that the document is actually a solemn declaration, what you call "zakletva" is a solemn declaration, so there is no way we can talk about a pledge or an oath and that's why I'm asking you why do you insist on using the term which does not have any foundation either in the law or in any other document, save for the document -- the contents of which are dubious and provide false characterisation of some indisputable facts?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a thesaurus handy, but I believe that a pledge, oath, and solemn declaration - at least in English, which is the language I wrote my report in - are all synonyms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I know, however you speak the Serbian language and it should be absolutely clear to you that there is a major difference in the Serbian language between what the Serbs call "zakletva" or "pledge" and "svecana izjava" or solemn declaration, am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to tender this document for admission, 65 ter 77?

utterances.speaker: MR. DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- could we know what the difference is then in ... because you -- obviously you know what the difference is in your language and the expert knows, but do we know?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, 18, 21, does not reflect the witness's answer, so I'm going to use this moment and clarify the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, I know that you speak the Serbian language, that's what I referred to, and I suggested that you were aware of the terms "svecana izjava" and "zakletva" in the Serbian language and you answered the question, and now the Judge has kindly asked you to clarify the difference. Could you please first answer the question again, I believe that your answer was yes, and then could you please provide an explanation as to what the difference between the two terms is in the Serbian language in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry for overlapping with you. I would agree that there is a difference, I don't know that I would call it a major difference, but the term that you refer to as solemn oath is the term, the very specific term that is consistently used in the laws on internal affairs of both SRBiH MUP and RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Just -- I would just like to, because so far in this case we use the proper -- as the proper translation "solemn declaration," not the "solemn oath." So in order to distinct them to keep it in line with what we have, I ask you, please, to refer to solemn declaration as translation for "svecana izjava."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I take note of that and I agree that that is the most precise translation of the Serbian term.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: His Honour Judge Delvoie kindly asked you to try to explain the difference between the term "svecana izjava" and the term "oath," or "zakletva" in the Serbian language?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would certainly defer to a native speaker on this point, but my understanding is that the term "svecana izjava," solemn declaration is consistently used in the law where law enforcement and, for example, military officials swear duty allegiance to the organisation in which they will be employed. Whereas "zakletva" is used much more loosely and often outside official context. But I would, again, defer to a native speaker on the fine points of those two which often end up becoming pseudonyms in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think it would be proper for me to give evidence on that, so we will provide the explanation with some other witnesses, but I will make sure that this is clarified to the point where Your Honours will be able to understand the distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can I perhaps assist with the Oxford English dictionary on pledge, which is a solemn commitment to do or refrain from doing something, a promise. So I don't really see what your problem is when -- if in the report Mr. Nielsen uses the term "pledge" because I do think what your problem is with oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: But pledge does not have that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I referred to the distinction between loyalty, statement of loyalty or loyalty oath that the witness uses in his report, which I say is not correct. The second thing I take issue with the oath, declaration of oath, which I think is not right also. And that is the -- we say it's a solemn declaration like it says in the law and in all statements of the officials of RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think when I looked at my Oxford dictionary, I look for oath and one of the definitions was solemn declaration, so it seems like we go in a circle whichever point we start from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Isn't in the word "oath" also the fact that one invokes God with it, would that be the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think that may have been one of the alternative definitions was that sometimes there was a reference to God.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, in any case, the referential language here is Serbian or Serbo-Croat language and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's why I asked what it meant --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I understand fully, Your Honours. And we will make sure that this is explained to Your Honours properly at a certain point in time. Can we have this document exhibited, please. 65 ter 77.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D138, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After that document on the same date Mr. Zupljanin, the chief of the Banja Luka security services, responded to Minister Delimustafic in 65 ter 76, I believe that the document number is P34, and he repeats or that the allegations from the dispatch of the minister are not correct. Again, you will find that in your footnote 161. He says that the allegations are incorrect and that it was not about a loyalty pledge but just a solemn declaration, but let's not go over that again. This is just for everybody's reference. P34 is the document number. Sir, Mr. Nielsen, in your report you say that after that dispatch was sent and received and your position is that there was never an agreement between the political factors which composed the bodies of power at the time in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and in -- and the MUP on the other hand, about the division of MUP. And you state in one of the paragraphs of your expert report that because of the dispatch, amongst other things, on the 5th of April, Mr. Mandic was fired from the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that my position on that issue is slightly misquoted, but I'm happy to agree with you that Mr. Mandic was indeed fired from the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 5th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you know that Mr. Mico Stanisic was appointed and assigned to perform tasks and duties as an advisor in the office of Minister Delimustafic as of February 1992? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date of that appointment, but that's entirely possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you 1D00-2733. Just a moment. It's 47 in your tabs.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a decision on appointment, assignment should I say, of Mr. Mico Stanisic as advisor in the minister's cabinet in the Ministry of the Interior signed by Minister Alija Delimustafic. It's dated 14 February, but it relates to the period as of 10 February 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After that, Mico Stanisic was appointed minister in the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that Mr. Stanisic was never dismissed from the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, but then I also hope that he is getting his pension.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, if we were to consider that Mr. Stanisic has done something that is contrary to the law and the regulations of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I'm sure that some measures would have been taken under the law to discipline him?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was an attempt at the beginning of April 1992 to, as you put it, discipline those officers or officials of Serbian nationality who had left the ministry and formed RS MUP. However, I think in light of the difficult situation and the reality that such disciplinary measures could not be carried out, the Bosnian Muslim officials and Bosnian Croat officials who remained in MUP quickly stopped pursuing such matters. So it's entirely possible that Mr. Stanisic and others who went to RS MUP were never the formal subjects of disciplinary procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Nielsen, how do you then explain that they found the time to write a decision to dismiss Mr. Mandic and not the others, especially Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's quite clear that they probably prioritised the dismissal of Mr. Mandic because he is the one who sent that dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document as well, if there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D139.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, to support your claims about the non-existence of agreement to divide the MUP, you cite in footnote 135 and paragraph 92 some reaction on the ground, specifically the dispatch from the public security station of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 65 ter 326. I believe it has also a number in e-court, but I'm told there is a problem with uploading. It's document P179.18. The title was not put in correctly or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You cite this document in support of your theory; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cite the document as a relevant document and I recall that we dealt with this on direct examination, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, since you worked in the research section of the Office of the Prosecutor you are aware that the division of the public security station of Zvornik happened on the 6th of April?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the precise date but I think that's quite correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the 28th and 29th March there occurred a problem in the public security station of Zvornik when the assistant commander invited members of the public security station of Tuzla to come and provide security in the public security station of Zvornik. His name was Adnan Karovic; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I know that, and I know that there were a tremendous amount of problems at SJB Zvornik during this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document, the second signatory is one Dragan Spasojevic. You will see his name under Osman Mustafic and that was the chief of SJB?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the document could be scrolled down just a little bit. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that already on the 6th of April, the Crisis Staff of Zvornik or the provisional government, as it was called, he was -- appointed him the commander of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you then explain his signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should think that's a question that's more appropriate for Mr. Spasojevic than for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree. Mr. Nielsen, would you cast your mind back to the document 1D78. Isn't it the case that you were present and even actively involved in taking the statement from Mr. Cedo Kljajic, assistant minister of the interior of Republika Srpska in 1992 for public security?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I participated in taking a statement from Mr. Cedo Kljajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that interview, I suppose, since it was held in The Hague, as indicated on the document, must have been conducted in this building, I suppose, and it took three days?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, you put a certain number of questions to Mr. Cedo Kljajic. Isn't it the case that more than 50 per cent of that document is devoted to the issue of the division of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that we discussed that topic. I don't know that that constitutes more than 50 per cent of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it the case, Mr. Nielsen, that in the course of that interview, Mr. Cedo Kljajic more than once not only confirmed that it was done with the agreement of all the relevant organs and individuals in the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but pointed specifically to this document from the MUP collegium of the 1st of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of years has passed since I spoke with Mr. Kljajic, but I believe that that is probably quite accurate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In that case, I have to ask you again, why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, just one moment. Is it correct that in your question you said that in the course of that interview, Mr. Kljajic, more than once not only confirmed that it was done with agreement of all the relevant organs and individuals in the MUP of the Serbian republic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Thank you, Your Honour. What I said is [Interpretation] MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That was the real name at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was saying, Mr. Nielsen, bearing all that in mind including these facts, don't you find, or rather, wouldn't you agree with me that in the light of all that has been said a moment ago, and in the light of this document, your failure to include that document in your report, or comment upon it in any way, or refer to it in any way, constitutes a rather serious omission in your report?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, that's argumentative. He has already said he should have included it in his report. It's up to you judges to decide at the end of the case how much weight to give that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Thank you very much. [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have completed this part of my cross-examination of Mr. Nielsen. I thank you, Mr. Nielsen, I will continue later, and now my colleague Mr. Cvijetic will pick up the next topic. Thank you. Perhaps, Your Honour, we could take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one administrative matter before the witness is ushered into the courtroom. There was two days ago a document which was marked for identification, 1D116. If you remember, Your Honours, the point of the matter was that the third page of the document did not correspond to the previous two pages. Now, we have -- what we did is we filed a third page as 1D01-1052 document, and we would like that this document be connected with 1D116 as a number of exhibit and the document be admitted now if there's no objection, fully admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Nielsen, my name is Slobodan Cvijetic. I'm a co-counsel on the Defence team of Mr. Stanisic. In this cross-examination I will deal with one particular topic from your report, the one you called the Law on the Interior of Republika Srpska. Within that topic, willy-nilly, we'll have to run through a couple of systemic regulations in order to be able to understand the character, the place, the role, and the jurisdiction of such an important organ of state administration, and of course we'll devote the bulk of our time to the Law on Internal Affairs. And finally, to internal regulatory documents of the Ministry of the Interior, that the minister of the interior was duty-bound under the law to enact in order to regulate everything that the law objectively is not able to. So let us take things in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, just one moment. Could I state for the record that I'm not Judge Hall. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can all see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Like you did, I'll start with the constitution of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, your footnote 148, 150, 151, that's where you mentioned these so-called systemic regulations, and I will start immediately with the constitution to see how the constitution defines the role in the place of the Ministry of the Interior within the system of state administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 65 ter 49, exhibited as P181.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting to see it on the screen, it's the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina which, as I suppose you know, the Assembly of Republika Srpska adopted on the 28th of February 1992. The relevant article we need is 69, and for the Registry, in B/C/S it's page 6, in English it's page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour, I had forgotten the binder, can I ask the usher to give it to the witness? I put for him all the documents in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Number 5. Article 69. As you can see, the constitution defines this well known division of power. You know that in parliamentary systems, there is a division into the judiciary, legislative, and executive power. We see that executive power is given to the government, therefore we'll not waste time on that and we'll look instead at Article 90 to see what the constitution says about the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 7 in B/C/S and 15 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I suppose, Mr. Nielsen, you have already found it. And you can look also at 92 if they can fit on the screen at the same time. 90 and even better 92, and 92 in English. You will agree with me that the constitution deals with the government very tersely and practically enumerates only in this article who constitutes the government, the prime minister, deputy prime ministers, and ministers. We are not going to deal with it much, just to invoke the law as you did. Let's move to Article 97 for my first question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 8 in B/C/S and 16 in English. Can we perhaps zoom in on Article 97.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is what we need. Here we see that the constitution placed the ministries of the government within republic organs of administration. Ministries, including Ministry of the Interior are state agencies and they are executive power. The state administration.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, and good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You are right, I didn't give you a chance to say that before. This is all we need about the definition from the constitution. Let us now look at the next regulation, which you refer to in footnote 150, that's the Law on the Government.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need now 1D01-1017.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, you are on the border-line of the expertise of this witness by invoking the constitution and the laws, and when I suggested this morning that counsels should endeavour to get straight to the point, it was -- it was incidents just such as this that I had in mind. I do not believe that it will be beneficial to the Chamber to have this witness explain much about the law to us, so my question to you here and now is if you would be so kind as to tell us where do you want to go with this in relation to Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise for failing to say this in my introduction to the witness. I am aware that this witness is not a lawyer, but in his 30 or 40 pages of his report, he deals with legal issues. I forgot to stress to him that I will deal with legal issues only up to the level up to which he dealt with them in his report. I'm not going to ask for expert opinion from the field of constitutional law and law in general. The purpose of this line of questioning is only to establish the proper place of the Ministry of the Interior among organs of state administration under the laws and regulations. The witness himself dealt with these regulations in his report. We will only go into detail about the Law on Internal Affairs, which the witness did himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. But my question would be is this a contested matter between the parties? Is that something that we need to address at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is one regulation that Mr. Nielsen did not refer to, whereas it is the regulation which best defines the scope and especially the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Interior. I think he omitted one regulation and that's the one I want to put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, but I'm curious as to what you want to show by drawing the witness's attention to the fact that he may have omitted one particular regulation. What is the significance of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, immediately after that I will put to him a question asking him to agree with my conclusion about the definition of organs, their role, and the form of leadership. In order to put that question, I have to go through this a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let's get on with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, we will develop on the Law on Government for no more than 15 seconds, just enough to look at Article 6, and you will agree with me that there's nothing there but the fact that that article lists the ministries within the government starting with the Ministry of the Interior, as you will certainly agree with me. Am I right in saying all this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, and I would add that I think it is very interesting that Internal Affairs is listed first on the list of ministries.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We'll have to break for two minutes just to permit Judge Hall to come in. --- Break taken at 11.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning, I apologise for the interruption but let the record show that we are now fully constituted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please, continue Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, could you please be shown Exhibit 1D01-1024. Mr. Nielsen, it will be number 7 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see page number 1 in B/C/S. There's no English version. This is one of the documents which entered the library of legal documents that has to be agreed upon with the OTP. It has been long in the offing. Since the witness speaks our language we are going to using article just one article from this law, we should be done with this law very quickly. This is the law on ministers. Mr. Nielsen, you will agree with me that you omitted to take a look at that regulation, but it's neither here nor there. Could you please look at Roman II dealing with republican administration bodies, and you will see a list of all the different ministries, and then in Article 8 which starts on this page and goes on -- continues on the following page, you will assist us as well as the Trial Chamber -- you will agree with me when I say that this is the first law that describes in detail the authorities, tasks, and duties of these particular ministries and what it is supposed to do within its purview. Could you please look at that article, I believe that it's quite elaborate, and will you agree with me in all that I've just said?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that it is relevant for Internal Affairs. I agree with you that I should have cited it because it is relevant for Internal Affairs. I agree with that you Article 8 deals with the remit and ambit of the Ministry of the Interior, and I would point out -- now whether it's the first or second matter issued, it's certainly issued on the same day that the Law on Internal Affairs is issued, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nielsen. Can I just summarise all the regulations. I'm not going to deal with the Law on State Administration that you studied. Can we then agree that the Ministry of the Interior was one of the administration bodies headed by the minister in charge of that body. Would that be the shortest possible definition of this particular body?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. And I believe it's the Law on State Administration that says that minister is in charge of the ministry, which is a logical point.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And that it manages that body as one of the administrative bodies?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As I have already promised the Trial Chamber, I will move on to your report now without any further ado. I will move on to paragraphs 95, 96, 97, and 98 of your report. And I will also move on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: With all due respect, I apologise for interrupting you again, but may I ask if the whole point of this exercise was just to show that the ministry is a part of the administration and it is headed by a minister?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only that. I also wanted to demonstrate the way that body was managed, how it was administered. That part is also relevant to us. And later on we will elaborate that issue further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we have learned much about how it was administered other than the fact at that it was administered according to the law, and I suppose that the law will not provide any different provisions from what is normally applicable to a ministry in a modern state. So, so far I have seen no surprise. And, again, my question is if this is not a contested matter between the parties, then I really think that we should not have used and spent any time on this. So my advice again to parties on both sides is to focus on the point that are contested, that are at issue here otherwise we'll never get to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to indicate with regard to whether it's a contested issue or not, the constitution and the Law on Internal Affairs and the Law on Ministries and State Administration are all part of the law library that we put together that have stipulation, but we don't contest the contents of these laws, so I don't think it's necessary to ask the witness about what it says. It says what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the parties do not agree on the way that body was administered and managed. This will be the point of my cross-examination when I come to that part, and you will understand why it was very important for me to clarify that matter with the witness and how things were positioned at the time. May I proceed with the Law on Internal Affairs, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, I have already referred to the relevant paragraphs in your report. I would like to focus on paragraph 97 first of all. In this paragraph you claim, as we can all read, or you provide a comment on the Law on Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska, rather, and you say that it's provisions are in keeping with the remarks of Goran Zugic, the Bosnian Serb who worked at the security services in Tuzla, and you quote things from his letter. Mr. Nielsen, when it comes to this letter by Mr. Zugic do you consider it a serious source for the wording and the provisions of the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would specify so that we are clear that I don't cite a letter of Mr. Zugic, rather I cite his comment at the meeting of Bosnian Serb police officials at a meeting that we previously discussed on the 11 of February 1992, which is, of course, prior to the promulgation of the RS Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, I apologise. Well, yes, yes, but look at your own text, it says that the provisions of the Law on Internal Affairs are in accordance or in keeping with Mr. Zugic's remark. This is the part that I was referring to in my question, and if you want me to be more specific, let me ask you this: Did Goran Zugic's words have an impact on the wording and the text of certain provisions in this law, that's my specific question to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That calls for speculation on the part of this witness to know what the drafters of the law knew about what Mr. Zugic said. I think that's beyond his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The witness can express this by himself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Cvijetic, when I write that comment what I mean is that there are indications that certain elements in the Law on Internal Affairs, by no means all of the Law on Internal Affairs of the Republika Srpska but certain elements in it, bear traces from an analytical point of view of having stemmed from previously expressed concerns and dissatisfactions of Bosnian Serbs in SRBiH MUP as regards the previous Law on Internal Affairs that stem from 1990, and I can give a very specific example of that: The Bosnian Serbs, as I state in my report, were actively seeking the establishment of a new Security Services Centre in Trebinje, in Eastern Herzegovina. Such a Security Services Centre was not provided for in the 1990 law, but was provided for in the 1992 law which the Bosnian Serb Assembly drafted and passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, Mr. Nielsen, I apologise. My question was very specific and could you provide a specific answer to it. Did it and to what extent did Mr. Zugic's words have any impact on the drafting of this law and the text of this law, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether his words personally had any effect, I do not know. I do know that the thoughts that he expressed are evident in the new law.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot but ask you that, would you say that the complete procedure proceeding the passing of this law and what you told us yesterday and the day before yesterday on examination-in-chief and on cross-examination when you are talking about the transformation of the MUP, the [indiscernible] that was under the influence of the positions of the aforementioned gentleman?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer to your question is I believe that the drafting -- the transformation of the MUP and the drafting of the new Law on Internal Affairs of the RS was under the influence of the persons who participated at the 11 February 1992 meeting and that Goran Zugic was one of the participants at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well, we have to go back to paragraphs 96 and 98 in your report. One before and one after 97 where you say openly that a new Law on Internal Affairs is mostly based on the extricated text of the Law on Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, this is what you say in 1998. My very specific question to you - and I'm calling for a yes or no answer: When you look at paragraphs 96 and 98, would you say that your paragraph 97 contradicts what you say in paragraphs 96 and 98?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not at this point see a contradiction, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I will take that as a valid answer. We can't agree on everything, can we. I will now move on to paragraph 99 in your report. We'll stay with it very briefly. You state in this paragraph, Mr. Nielsen, that one of the main and most obvious differences between the two laws concerns terminology. Will you agree with me when I say that it is the least important of all differences?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree. I think it's significant and that they change these terms given that they were so closely leaning up against the 1990 law, I don't see anything specifically related to the RS in doing this. They are actually doing the same thing that lawyers all across eastern Europe are doing at that point; namely, removing references to, for example, working peoples' and replacing them with citizens which reflects a transition from a socialist political system, a party state system, to a multi-party system in which the old socialist provisions are no longer present.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, that was the essence of my suggestion when I said that only that terminological difference had its basis in the title of the former republican secretariat which resounds with socialist connotations in the law. And would you go to that issue, could you please tell me, I'm sure you know because you peruse so many documents, on all the documents issued by the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Mr. Delimustafic signs his name and precedes it with the title of minister; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and that reflects a de facto change because he should have signed as secretary according to the 1990 law.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The essence of my remark is that that terminology should not be given that much importance and significance; am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He can say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR.  HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's argumentative. He's the expert, he wrote the report, he decides how much weight to give it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you have made the minister title next to Mr. Delimustafic's name a very relative term, although the law is explicit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think it's a -- it's certainly a difference. Let us agree that it is a difference between the 1990 and 1992 laws, and then you and I may disagree about whether it's a significant difference or a less significant difference, but I think we both agree that it's a difference in the letter of the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. In my view, it is not very significant, particularly in terms of terminology --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But we can agree to disagree can't we.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's something for submission at the end of the case. It's not appropriate for him to make those kind of comments when he's addressing the witness. His opinion he keeps to himself until it's time to make presentations to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic, let's go on. Move on, next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept Your Honours and I will move on indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to paragraph 101. In this paragraph you deal with the links that the Law on Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska establishes. Have you found it? Oh, you are looking for the law. And you deal with the same matter in Articles 2, 22, 23, you deal with the same matter in all those articles, and the matter at hand are the way you define or the, rather, the way the law defines links between the Ministry of the Interior and federal bodies in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Let me remind you that at the moment when this law was passed, Yugoslavia was still in existence; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree with you. I would just like to ask if you could tell me which tab the law is at?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, please. Just briefly. Are you looking for the Law on Internal Affairs? I apologise, I thought that you already had it before you. It's number 1. That's what you should be looking for. Look at Article 2 and this is where you mention that link. Look also at Article 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I'm rushing, I have neglected to inform the Trial Chamber of the document number. It is 1D01-1112. No, that's not the document. It is the former 65 ter 1D01--- yes, yes, it's coming. Yes, very well. Excellent. Now we are where we should be. And for the time being in both versions, we will need the same page, page number 1. And we are looking at Article number 1, paragraph number 1 in that article. That's it. Thank you. I apologise, I only need to look at Article 2 which is already on the screen. In Article 2 you are dealing with the link, there is just one question in respect of all the three articles. Can we now look at Articles 22 and 23, which are both on page 3 in both the English and the B/C/S versions of the text. That's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: These are the relevant provisions. And you are pointing to the fact that there is a link between the ministry and federal bodies. My question to you was whether at that moment Yugoslavia still existed and you will agree with me that Bosnia and Herzegovina were still not an internationally recognised state, that it was still an integral part of Yugoslavia, and if that is true, then these provisions should not constitute something that would point to something that is not in keeping with the regulations, as it were?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, and I do not say that these provisions are in violation with other regulations. I point out in paragraph 101 that this was a logical provision given the public claims of the RS leadership that they wished to maintain relations with the Yugoslav state and federal officials based in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You also agree with me that we could also look at the constitution and conclude that this is within the remit of the constitution. I don't know whether it is necessary for us to look at Article 3 in the constitution, Your Honours, where it says that the republic is an integral part of the federal state of Yugoslavia. Is that correct? You have the constitution before you. Maybe we should actually open the constitution and look at Article 3, that will confirm that the link between the republican ministry and the federal institution is not against the constitution. The document number is P181, and in your binder it's tab 5, I believe, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that that is what Article 3 of the constitution says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And also can we look at Article 143 in the constitution which is on page 10 in the B/C/S version and in English it is on page 23. We are looking at transitional or final provisions in paragraph 143. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me -- let's just see whether that page is on the screen, you will agree with me that the constitution and so on and so forth -- you will agree with me that the provisions of the constitution are reflected on the Law on the Interior allowing for all sorts of options in the political resolution to the crisis in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. All options are open for Yugoslavia to remain as it was, for Bosnia to be a new state. These final provisions allow for all those options and those options, possible options, are reflected on the Law on Internal Affairs, will you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree with you that that is what Article 143 of the constitution says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Would you then agree with me that all these provisions concerning links with federal organs of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia continued to exist in the laws of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and their application continued in the territory that was not under the control of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with you that the officials of the RS regarded the federal organs of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and its laws to continue to exist on the territory under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Nielsen, my question had do with the provisions of the Law on Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. They also kept these provisions on links with federal organs; they have been copied. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, and I believe that's what I state in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now move to your report. Paragraph 151. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You deal with Articles 37 and 38. Have you located of paragraph 121 of your report?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: That's what I said, 121. It may have been misinterpreted. 121.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm at 121.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So we'll focus on Article 37 of the law from 1990, and that's also Article 38 of the Law on Internal Affairs. You'll have to look at them in parallel. It's your number 1 and in tab 2 you have the other law. We want to focus on Article 38. The Law on Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's see if we have it on the screen. It's 1D01-1112. And in B/C/S we need page 5. And in English page 6. The Law on Internal Affairs. Very good. Thirty-eight, and in B/C/S it's on page 5. Could we just see 38 in B/C/S. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, since the Trial Chamber cannot follow both the laws at the same time, we'll have to see this provision in the Law on Republika Srpska and then go back to the law on the -- of the socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and detect the differences. It concerns certain restrictions envisaged by this article with the onset of extraordinary circumstances endangering the law and order. It says that minister may ban the assembly of people and movements of people in public places, or in a public place?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree with you that that is what Article 38 says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And in your comment on this provision you say that the difference between these two provisions is that the Law of Republika Srpska does not envisage the possibility of appeal by citizens whose movement and assembly is limited in this way, whereas appeal is possible in the law, in the 1990 law of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This comment is towards the end of paragraph 121 in your report. So the difference is that the Republika Srpska law does not provide for any possibility of appeal.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I state that that is a difference in the two versions of Article 38, that those portions to which you referred, Article 38 in the 1990 law, are excised from the 1992 law Article 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, that's precisely the purpose of my cross-examination.
